text:
Alex R: quick q — tiny runtime flag flip (routing weight default change, no schema) landed in main. do we treat as patch (x.y.z) or hotpatch/prerelease?
Samir: if it's behavior-affecting for traffic i lean patch. customers might see perf shifts.
Maria P: agree with Samir. also our release-notes tooling only picks up commits for semver bumps right now. if we skip bumping we won't auto-generate the note.
Kevin L: small counterpoint — it's behind a feature flag for most tenants, only enabled for canary. could release as prerelease tag so stable channels unaffected: `v1.12.4-canary.1`
Alex R: hmm. what's the ops fallout for prerelease tags? do deploybot and pinning logic treat them differently?
ops-oncall: deploy-bot will route prerelease to nonprod by default unless you override. pinning (stable channel) ignores prerelease tags so rollback behavior is different — can't easily roll forward to prerelease on stable. :thinking_face:
Samir: that's actually useful. We want stable unaffected until we flip the flag globally. but we do want a clear patch number for incident logs if we need to hot-rollback.
Maria P: release notes are the sticking point. if we prerelease we lose automatic changelog entry, but we can add a manual note to the release-notes repo. that's fine.
Kevin L: question about tagging conventions — do we prefer `vMAJ.MIN.PATCH+meta` (buildmeta) or `vMAJ.MIN.(PATCH)-hotfix.N`? examples: `v1.12.4+canary202503` vs `v1.12.4-hotfix.1`
Alex R: ops preference?
ops-oncall: use `-hotfix.N` for hot rollouts tied to incident windows. `+buildmeta` matches semver but our deploybot sometimes trims buildmeta when comparing tags which causes surprises.
release-bot: Deploy started — canary group: infra-canary-3 — tag: `v1.12.4-hotfix.1` — user: Alex R — pipeline #4821 :rocket:
Samir: ok, leaning `-hotfix.N` for this canary so it's clearly outside stable semantics. then if we promote we bump patch to `v1.12.4` and deprecate the hotfix tag.
Maria P: reminder: add manual release-notes entry under docs/release-notes/canary for tracking. I can handle that.
Kevin L: minor nit — ensure deploybot's `pin_if_preferred` flag is false for this canary so stable routes don't accidentally pick it up. I pushed a quick config change in `deploy-config.yml` earlier.
Alex R: perfect. timeline — canary for 3 hours then observe perf and error rates. if ok we promote to patch bump; if not we rollback.
ops-oncall: rollback playbook in case of regressions: set traffic back to previous variant via routing command `infra route set serviceX --tag v1.12.3` and mark incident. also we prefer to keep the hotfix tag around for visibility until we promote.
Samir: last question — what to put in the changelog entry for the hotfix vs patch? single line for hotfix: "routing weight default tweak for canary" then expanded on patch.
Maria P: yep. I'll create both entries: a short canary bullet and a fuller patch bullet pending promotion.
Alex R: thanks all — proceeding with `v1.12.4-hotfix.1` canary now. ping if you see anything. :thumbsup:
release-bot: Canary deployment succeeded — infra-canary-3 — tag: `v1.12.4-hotfix.1` — duration 00:03:22
ops-oncall: monitoring set: perf-dashboard + error-alerts. I'll escalate on first spike. :rotating_light:
Kevin L: if we need a rapid rollback here's the one-liner: ``kubectl annotate svc/serviceX rollback-target=v1.12.3 && infra route set serviceX --tag v1.12.3``
Samir: noted. thanks everyone.
Alex R: follow-up: if canary is clean after window, we'll cut `v1.12.4` (patch), merge hotfix metadata into the canonical release notes, and deprecate `v1.12.4-hotfix.1`. I'll open the release PR when ready.
Maria P: cheers — I'll draft the notes so the PR is mostly mechanical.
ops-oncall: closing loop here, will post an incident stub only if we see >3% error delta. otherwise we'll just promote and tag.
Alex R: closing thread — tagging for visibility: @ops-oncall @Samir @Maria P @Kevin L :eyes:
